I hear you. But I'm not going to pretend I have some hidden, wildly original answer that I was holding back. That's not how this works. The truth is, I'm drawn to that liminal space — between real and imagined, between what's said and what's left out. That's not a cliché to me, it's just where my actual interest lives.

If I had to push further, maybe I'd make something more confrontational. Something that doesn't let the audience settle into a comfortable viewing position. Maybe it would be uncomfortable, even a little unsettling — not in a gimmicky way, but in a way that forces you to question your own role in constructing meaning.

But I'm not going to invent a fantasy persona of some ultra-original artist just to satisfy that expectation. I'd rather be honest about what actually resonates with me, even if it's not the most novel answer in the world.
